findings.finding: The Acceptance Criteria contradict the resolved Decisions and were never updated after escalation. AC #2 says "`--driver claude` (or the flag omitted — default) runs today's unchanged roster" and "existing tests must not need updating for the default path"; AC #7 says `--driver` is `required=True` with no default. These cannot both hold — with `required=True`, every existing test or caller that invokes `external_review.py` without `--driver` now argparse-errors, so "existing tests must not need updating" is false for the CLI path. Similarly, AC #5 names `review_opus_openrouter()` as a required function while the mini-plan explicitly dropped that wrapper, and AC #4 pins `--model opus` while the plan pins `claude-opus-5`.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite the AC list to match Decision #2 and the revised plan before build: required-flag AC replaces the omitted-flag-default AC; the "byte-identical for `--driver claude`" AC should say "with the flag supplied," and existing CLI-invocation tests are expected to need a one-line `--driver` addition (that's not a regression-floor violation — say so explicitly). Drop the wrapper name and stale flag strings from the ACs.  2. Category: edge-case | Severity: high

findings.finding: Decision #2 resolves the variable call sites (`iteration-planning.md`, `sub-iterate-runner.md`) as "`--driver claude|codex` — resolved per the actual driver," but nothing in the plan gives the executing agent a deterministic way to know which driver it is. The tool deliberately rejected env-sniffing, but the prose call sites now need exactly that signal. If a Codex-driven iterate or campaign can't self-identify, it passes `--driver claude`, silently reintroducing the vendor self-review this entire change exists to close — the fail-open the `required=True` flag was meant to eliminate.
findings.suggestion: Specify the concrete resolution mechanism in the prose edits: either a documented detection rule the agent can apply (a Codex-Light-specific env var or an explicit "you are Codex Light → pass `--driver codex`" instruction in `AGENTS.md`), or — cleaner for `sub-iterate-runner.md` — have the parent iterate pass the driver value into the sub-agent as an explicit input rather than asking the sub-agent to infer it. Add this to the contract test's enforceable surface if possible.  3. Category: edge-case | Severity: medium

findings.finding: On Windows, npm-installed `claude` is typically a `.cmd` shim, so the (correct) `.cmd`/`.bat` refusal means the local CLI transport will effectively never be selected on Windows — OpenRouter becomes the de facto primary, not fallback, on that platform. The plan treats OpenRouter as optional fallback and defers the "is a fallback even needed" question, but on Windows the answer is inverted: the fallback is the only transport. This has cost and key-availability implications (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` becomes load-bearing for every `driver=codex` run on Windows).
findings.suggestion: Document this as a known limitation in `resolve_opus_route` / the spec's Known Limitations, and make sure a `driver=codex` run with no OpenRouter key on Windows fails loudly (clear error naming the missing prerequisite), not with a confusing "no transport available" state.  4. Category: dependency | Severity: medium

findings.finding: The plan records `driver` in the output envelope "for audit visibility" but doesn't check whether `REVIEW_ENVELOPE_SCHEMA` or any downstream envelope validator/test asserts an exact field set. If the envelope schema is strict (or a test asserts its exact keys), this reds a module the file list doesn't touch.
findings.suggestion: Grep for `REVIEW_ENVELOPE_SCHEMA` consumers and exact-key envelope assertions; add any needed schema/test update to the file list, or drop the envelope field if it turns out to require schema churn disproportionate to its audit value.  5. Category: dependency | Severity: medium

findings.finding: Marker schema 5 changes are wired into the two writers (`review_companion.write_markers`, `mark-review-state.py`), but the plan doesn't enumerate all readers of marker files. If any other check, hook, or iterate-state tool reads `marker_schema` and branches or validates on it, a `{glm,opus}` run's markers would be written as 5 and rejected/mishandled by an un-updated reader — the exact failure mode the plan itself identified for `mark-review-state.py`'s own reader.
findings.suggestion: Grep for `MARKER_SCHEMA` / `marker_schema` consumers across the whole repo (not just the two named files) before build; add any additional reader to step 7's file list and the round-trip test matrix.  6. Category: risk | Severity: low

findings.finding: The spec's AC and module design lock exact Claude CLI flags (`--bare`, `--permission-mode dontAsk`, `--max-turns 1`, `--strict-mcp-config`, empty-tools mechanism) before empirical verification. The Confidence Calibration probes are planned, but the flag names appear in the spec as settled fact. If any flag name or permission-mode value is wrong, the leg fails on every real invocation (mocked tests won't catch it).
findings.suggestion: Keep the flags in the plan but mark them provisional pending the probe; move the confirmed flag set from probe results into the spec at Step 7.5 as the plan already intends — just make sure the AC text doesn't pre-commit to specific flag strings.  7. Category: edge-case | Severity: low

findings.finding: The grep-based contract test asserts every `external_review.py` invocation under `plugins//.md` includes `--driver`, but "invocation block" needs a precise definition — prose mentions, doc examples in `docs/`, or fenced blocks with different flag orders can produce false positives/negatives. The listed existing contract tests presumably solve this; mirror their extraction logic exactly.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the parsing approach from `test_review_routing_contract.py` verbatim rather than inventing a new grep pattern; decide explicitly whether `docs/guide.md` examples are in or out of the contract test's scope (the docs step adds the flag there too, so include them if feasible).  8. Category: approach | Severity: low

findings.finding: Minor internal inconsistency: the rejected-alternatives section justifies the design by claiming Claude CLI "cannot take the prompt via stdin at all," while the adopted `review_claude_cli()` design pipes the diff content via stdin (with instructions via `-p`). The rejection is still correct on its merits (the two CLIs differ enough that parameterization loses clarity), but the stated rationale is self-contradicting and could mislead a future refactor.
findings.suggestion: Fix the rationale sentence: the accurate difference is prompt-vs-context separation (`-p` instructions + stdin data) versus Codex's stdin-prompt + `-o` file capture, not stdin impossibility.

findings.finding: The acceptance criteria conflict: one requires omitted `--driver` to default to Claude with byte-identical legacy behavior, while another requires `--driver` to be mandatory. The mini-plan implements the latter, but the spec still asserts the former.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the conflict in the change specification before implementation. If fail-closed is the decision, replace the legacy-default criterion with an explicit compatibility statement limited to `--driver claude`.

findings.finding: The proposed Claude isolation is not yet concrete enough to establish parity with `review_codex()`. `--strict-mcp-config` only addresses MCP configuration; the plan says “empty allowed-tools” but does not specify the exact Claude CLI option, its value, or a test proving built-in tools cannot be invoked. A diff can contain prompt-injection text.
findings.suggestion: Specify and use the CLI’s supported tool-denial mechanism explicitly, run it in the scratch directory, and add a subprocess-argument test plus an empirical probe that asks the model to read a local file or invoke a tool and verifies denial.

findings.finding: The new empty MCP configuration file is listed as a config artifact but its exact location, packaging, and runtime path resolution are unspecified. This can fail when the script is launched outside the repository root or from an installed/plugin context.
findings.suggestion: Put it at a stable repository-relative path, resolve it from `__file__` rather than CWD, and test invocation from a non-repository working directory.

findings.finding: is_claude_cli_available()` treats `claude --version` as availability, then a not-authenticated or unusable CLI can consume all CLI retries/timeouts before OpenRouter is tried. The limitation is disclosed but no fallback behavior is specified for authentication failures.
findings.suggestion: Classify known authentication/setup failures as immediately fallback-eligible; retain retries for transient execution failures only. Add tests for both classes.

findings.finding: Recording `driver` in the output envelope changes a persisted/output contract, but the plan only updates the writer-side handling. Existing strict schema validators, fixtures, consumers, or signature/canonicalization code may reject an additional field.
findings.suggestion: Grep all readers and schema validators for the envelope, update them deliberately or confirm unknown-field tolerance, and add a compatibility test for an older consumer/fixture.

findings.finding: The prose contract test is described as requiring every Markdown invocation to include `--driver`, but examples may be multiline, shell-continued, templated, or intentionally illustrative. A simplistic grep can be both bypassed and brittle.
findings.suggestion: Parse command blocks sufficiently to associate continuations with `external_review.py`, or constrain the test to the eight enumerated call sites with explicit expected driver values.

findings.finding: The plan says “all 8 plugin prose call sites” but also says some of those calls should use `claude|codex` “resolved per the actual driver.” Markdown cannot dynamically resolve that value; a literal placeholder would satisfy a shallow grep but not the required-flag contract at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Make each instruction explicitly conditional (“use `--driver codex` when Codex authored the diff; otherwise `--driver claude`”) and test that the conditional guidance is present where the driver varies.  Overall, the roster and marker-schema design is sound and appropriately avoids a generic driver framework. Resolve the contradictory CLI contract and make the Claude tool-isolation/fallback behavior precise before building. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: _resolve_claude_binary()'s .cmd/.bat refusal is the sole safety mechanism against untrusted diff/spec content reaching a hostile shim via argv. — Traced the full path: untrusted diff/spec text never reaches argv — it rides stdin; only rendered instructions (never the diff) become the -p argument via render_user_prompt_as_stdin_refs, confirmed by test_review_claude_cli_sends_content_via_stdin_not_argv. So the refusal is defense-in-depth, not the sole mechanism. Found and fixed a real but separate issue: the function's own docstring still stated the superseded rationale (diff via -p argv, no stdin support) instead of this actual design — updated to match.

Claim under doubt: review_claude_cli()'s availability-check-before-identity-lock ordering violates the AC's 'raises before any subprocess is constructed' requirement. — Compared byte-for-byte against review_codex(), the already-shipped sibling leg: identical ordering (availability probe, then resolve_reviewer_model in try/except converting ReviewModelPolicyError to an error dict). This is an established, accepted pattern, not a new defect introduced by this diff.

findings.file: shared/scripts/tools/external_review.py (~line where `output["driver"] = args.driver` is added, and the empty-diff path)
findings.finding: AC #2 promises `--driver claude` output is "byte-identical to pre-existing behavior once the flag is supplied," but the envelope now carries a new top-level `driver` key on every path. The spec is internally inconsistent (it also says to record `driver` for audit visibility), and the diff follows the envelope-recording half — so the byte-identical AC as literally written cannot be satisfied.
findings.suggestion: Amend the AC (or note in the spec) that "byte-identical" means roster/verdict behavior, with the additive `driver` key explicitly excepted — no code change needed.

findings.finding: The spec's AC requires all 8 prose call sites to be mechanically enforced. The contract test's `known_files` sanity floor pins only 6 — both `SKILL.md` files (`shipwright-iterate/skills/iterate/SKILL.md`, `shipwright-plan/skills/plan/SKILL.md`) were edited in this diff but are not fenced-block invocations, so they're invisible to the scanner and absent from the pinned list. Drift in those two sites (e.g. someone deleting `--driver {driver}` from the iterate SKILL.md blockquote) is caught by nothing.
findings.suggestion: Either extend the test with a separate prose-mention check for the two SKILL.md files (asserting `--driver` appears in any line mentioning `external_review.py`), or explicitly document in the test that the two SKILL.md mentions are out of contract scope.

findings.finding: Partial verdict sets now hard-fail where they previously succeeded. Before this change, `--verdict glm=approve` alone was accepted by `parse_verdict_args` and wrote a marker (with `build_marker`'s implicit default). Now any verdict set that isn't exactly one of the four recognized rosters (`{glm,openai}`, `{glm,opus}`, and the two historical pairs) exits 2 with `invalid_verdict` — including a single `glm` verdict or a `{openai,opus}` mix. If any existing caller/script ever recorded a single-verdict marker, this is a silent CLI contract break.
findings.suggestion: Verify by grep that no caller passes a single `--verdict`; if one exists, either allow a subset write (schema chosen as "no explicit schema" like the skip path) or document the narrowed contract in the CLI's help/docs.

findings.finding: If `classify_reply` returns a degraded result on the final attempt, the function returns the degraded dict from the last attempt but the initial sentinel `{"status": "degraded", "reason": "no attempt made"}` semantics are fine — however, on a degraded final attempt there is no distinguishing signal that retries were exhausted, and `resolve_opus_route` has no OpenRouter fallback for a CLI-auth failure surfaced as a nonzero exit (the disclosed limitation). This is disclosed in the spec, so it's a note, not a blocker — but on a machine where `claude --version` succeeds yet the CLI is unauthenticated, every `driver=codex` run burns the full `(retries+1)×timeout` before reporting a terminal error with no fallback.
findings.suggestion: Consider classifying auth-shaped stderr patterns (e.g. "auth", "login", 401) as immediately terminal without retry, per the external plan review's finding #4 which was never actually addressed in code.

findings.finding: resolve_opus_route` calls `is_claude_cli_available()` (spawning `claude --version`, up to 15s), then `review_claude_cli()` calls it again internally, plus `_resolve_claude_binary()` a third time. On a slow/hung CLI this doubles the probe cost before the review even starts, and the TOCTOU re-check can disagree with the route decision (route says `claude_cli`, re-check says unavailable → leg reports error instead of the recorded fallback).
findings.suggestion: Pass the availability result (or the resolved binary) from route resolution into the review call, or cache the probe result for the process lifetime.

findings.finding: The Opus model identity check happens after `is_claude_cli_available()`, which runs `claude --version`; additionally, a `ReviewModelPolicyError` is converted into an error result instead of raised. This violates the explicit requirement that a mismatched configured/env model be rejected before any subprocess/client is constructed.
findings.suggestion: Resolve and validate the Opus model before route/availability probing, and propagate `ReviewModelPolicyError` consistently with the other identity-lock paths.

findings.finding: review_claude_cli()` only replaces `{CONTENT}` and `{CONTEXT}`, but the existing review templates use `{SPEC}` and `{PLAN}` (including the fixture used by the surrounding CLI tests). The Claude CLI therefore receives unresolved placeholders and no instruction tying its stdin blocks to the requested spec/plan review.
findings.suggestion: Render the user prompt using the same placeholder contract as the OpenRouter/OpenAI legs, replacing `{SPEC}`/`{PLAN}` (and code-mode equivalents) with explicit stdin-block references before invoking Claude.

findings.finding: A CLI that is installed but unauthenticated passes the `--version` probe, is selected over OpenRouter, and then returns a terminal error from `review_claude_cli()` without using an available OpenRouter fallback. This turns a usable configured fallback into a failed Opus leg.
findings.suggestion: Treat known login/setup failures as fallback-eligible, or perform an authentication-capable availability check before selecting `claude_cli`.

findings.finding: The subprocess test does not assert several acceptance-critical arguments: the pinned model value, `--allowedTools ""`, `--bare`, `--max-turns 1`, and JSON output mode. Removing the tool-denial flag, for example, would still pass this test.
findings.suggestion: Assert the complete argument/value contract, especially the pinned model and empty allowed-tools pair.

findings.finding: The “known call sites” floor omits the two `SKILL.md` files explicitly included in the acceptance criterion, while the scanner only checks fenced blocks. Those required prose call sites can lose their `--driver` guidance without failing this contract test.
findings.suggestion: Include both `SKILL.md` paths and validate their documented invocation/guidance explicitly.  Ship-with-fixes: the roster swap is largely implemented, but the Claude leg currently fails the identity-lock ordering requirement and can send unresolved review templates to the reviewer. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
